updates.text: Secondary user types count everywhere: CL-Cancelled on the visit form (spelling-proof, Super Super Admin added), posting Announcements, My Profile schedule / Role-Department edits, Technician Performance import, and Training List's Branch Manager / Senior Manager pickers now check primary and secondary user types (shared anyHeldRoleIn)

Deactivated people show across the app as their name with a flag - "Jane Doe (Deactivated)" - instead of "— (Deactivated User)"; flagged once (a name already flagged is left alone). Pages with their own Deactivated badge still show the plain name; pickers still leave them out

Trainee Attendance keeps deactivated trainees' punched days (pending ones still reviewable) with their real name and a "Deactivated · date" flag (first deactivation); no "no punch" row for them. Signed PDFs: the capture turns off kerning / ligatures and waits for fonts, so text built on a phone no longer comes out with gaps ("Provide   a detailed", " :", "clock -in")

Absent List -> Exceeded -> Time Corrections: Warning Form column for people over the limit - the time-correction warning sent for that month (Warning Forms, and "Previous Warning(s) Issued" lines, worded about time corrections; filed under the month of the dates it's about), clickable to view the form near full screen; "Not sent" when there's none. Warned people stay at the top but aren't red, and drop out of the over-limit counts and the Exceeded / Time Corrections badges. HR Paperworks -> Warning Form flags sent 2nd warnings with no 1st listed (and 3rd with fewer than two), with a filter. AppModal gets a "full" size

Expenses: several receipts per expense (up to 10 photos / PDFs, each its own file) - pick many at once on the Self-Service / Accounting form and the mobile form, thumbnails with remove; Expenses table shows two thumbnails + "+N", Self-Service and mobile "View receipts (N)"; the receipt viewer gets Previous / Next (and arrow keys). First receipt stays in receipt_url, the rest in extra_receipts (migration 0414); removed and deleted receipts' files are cleaned up

Expenses: two tabs (Flash Tech, Employee Requests) - Flash Tech has color-coded All / Trips / Hotel / Car Rental / Allowance buttons with counts (Hotel and Car Rental moved in from their own tabs, covering trip and Accounting-added lines). New "Flash Tech / Allowance" type of reimbursement on the Self-Service and mobile forms (migration 0413) that lands under Flash Tech with Approve / Reject; Status and Approve / Reject otherwise only on employee requests. Branch filter and Branch column, Spend by branch bars (Most -> least / A -> Z, click to filter), redesigned summary cards (Total Spend / Records / Average / Largest where there's no status), compact rows with clickable Description, one-line actions, sideways scroll with a floating scrollbar

Expenses: Employee Requests gets an All / PH / US filter (PH = assigned branch Philippines) that the cards, list and CSV follow; Approve / Reject show only on employees' own expense requests - Flash Tech, Hotel and Car Rental are added straight by Accounting

PTO / Sick Leave balances deduct only APPROVED days - pending ones show beside the balance ("5/5 (3 pending)", "5 days left (3 days pending)") on the Master List (and its XLSX), HR Calendar, the balance under each PTO request's Type, Employee Self-Service and the mobile PTO form; Claims and CSR Team daily reports deduct approved only. A new request still can't go past what's left after the pending ones, and Absent List's Exceeded Sick Days still counts pending

Attendance Monitoring Report: Department Summary (Technician, CSR, Accounting, BizOps, Senior Managers, Triage, PO, Parts, Claims, IT, then any other role) - click a department to see its people with Department, Branch, Manager, Days Worked, Working Hours, Avg Hours / Day, Days Absent, Missing Time Out, Leave Days, Correction Requests (Approved / Pending / Rejected) and Warnings, also in the XLSX; headers centered over their counts. Deactivated accounts show with their real name and "Deactivated · date" (the first time they were deactivated), not counted absent from that day. HR Master List: Not Active rows and deactivated logins keep their real names, with a Deactivated · date flag next to the name

Accounting Dashboard payroll table: the Deactivated badge shows the date ("Deactivated · Oct 27, 2026") from User Management's Activity Log - the day it took effect when one was picked, else the day it was done; no date when none is logged

AHS Server Status -> AHS Updates (new card beside Server Status): every update made to the app, newest first - a short title, time, files changed and the update's ID, a summary line and Show details for the full message; search, Last 7 / 30 / 90 days / All time and the count of updates and files shown. Built from Angelo's, Jhon's and John Oliver's own repos by scripts/team-updates.cjs into src/lib/teamUpdates.json (loaded only when the page opens), counted by who made each change (merges and pulls of someone else's work left out). AHS Server Status opens to Admin and up (Admin / SuperAdmin / SuperSuperAdmin, primary or extra role) - the Home tile, both pages and the server's live checks; it was SuperAdmin only. PTO Requests (Attendance Monitoring and Employee Monitoring -> PTO Management): Reason and Photo columns - the employee's reason (3 lines, click for all) and the attached photo / PDF (opens in place), "-" when there's none. Self-Service PTO request: optional Photo or PDF (Sick / Unpaid Leave still require proof); a failed upload keeps the request and says so

Deactivated flag shows the deactivation date (Staff Form Checklist and User Management, from the Activity Log; accounts with no logged deactivation show no date); Angelo Mendoza's entries no longer show as the actor in User Management Status. PTO / leave filing: declared company holidays (Holiday Calendar) are not counted as leave days and a request that is only holidays (plus rest days) is refused; employees filing their own leave can't start PTO or Unpaid Leave on a past date, and Sick Leave must be filed at least 1 day ahead (HR plotting leave for someone is exempt). Migration 0407: SuperAdmin / SuperSuperAdmin may edit their own profile record (status, start date, branch, contact info etc.); account identity stays locked for everyone, other roles unchanged

Warning Form: a 2nd warning needs a 1st on file and a 3rd needs two (approved or pending warnings, plus sent forms not yet confirmed) - Preview & Send stays locked with a note, and "+ Add previous warning" opens with the missing one ticked; backfilled warnings now take a type (1st/2nd/3rd), saved as "1st Warning - reason" like confirmed ones. Deactivated accounts show as "- (Deactivated User)" across the app (display only, nothing stored changes; dropdown options are hidden) except Payroll, HR Paperworks, the signing pages, User Management and the Staff Form Checklist. Staff Form Checklist lists deactivated people with a Deactivated badge and an Account filter (All / Activated / Deactivated). User Management Status ignores Angelo Mendoza's activate/deactivate entries (still in the Activity Log). Exceeded Time Corrections: H (Holiday) column removed

Staff Form Checklist: "AHS Forms PH" tab next to PH Staff (Master PH Contractor Agreement, W-8BEN, Direct Deposit, Valid ID) - only the Master PH Contractor Agreement must be the version of the tab (PH Staff = US In Home Services, AHS Forms PH = Admin Hub Solutions); Direct Deposit, Valid ID and W-8BEN carry over between both; sends from the AHS tab go out as the AHS version. "Signed by" notifications for AHS copies open their AHS Forms PH tab; the PH agreement awaiting-employer badge counts each version on its own tab

HR Paperworks: "AHS Forms PH" group beside Onboarding - Master PH Contractor Agreement, Direct Deposit and Valid ID in their Admin Hub Solutions versions (AHS logo and name), plus Form W-8BEN. Original tabs are back to US In Home Services for everything on file; each copy keeps its version (form_data.brand) through filling, employer signature, Regenerate PDF and Regenerate all, and each tab lists only its own version. Master PH Contractor Agreement keeps its original title (Master Philippines Independent Contractor Comprehensive Agreement) in both versions. Valid ID send panel gets Preview

HR Paperworks: "Regenerate all PDFs" - pick any of the 15 regenerable forms (counts of signed copies shown), rebuild every signed copy with today's logo and layout keeping signatures, photos and answers, with a progress bar (current person, %, failures listed, Stop); skips cancelled, unsigned and scanned paper copies and Flash Travel signed under older wording; warns before forms with new wording (Direct Deposit, PH Agreement); logged in the Activity Log

Ticket Attachments: photo checklist by type - Model and Serial Number, Before-Work, After-Work, Invoice / Repair Order (required), Floor Mats, Existing Physical Damage, Part Being Replaced, Signs of Infestation (optional); each photo saved with its type (ticket page, mobile incl. offline, Pre-Claim summary), older photos can be given a type; Claims Readiness checks the 4 required types (tickets with only untyped photos keep the old rule). Direct Deposit and Valid ID: Admin Hub Solutions name and AHS logo. Master PH Contractor Agreement renamed Master Confidentiality, Non-Solicitation, and Affirmative Duty Agreement (shown as "... (PH)" in AHS) with Admin Hub Solutions and the AHS logo

Guides by department: General (Getting Started, Self-Service, Approving Requests) plus CSR, Triage, Logistics (Parts team), Claims and BizOps tiles, each with its own tours and shown to that department (Admin / SuperAdmin see all). New Claims ticket tour (Claims Readiness, product vs rating plate, photos, parts with invoices, Back Order vs NLA, visit log, Claim Transaction); look-only tours for filing a claim (Need Claim List -> Pre-Claim) and a complete Pre-Auth guide (also under BizOps). Pre-Auth: Part NLA (No Longer Available) per part line, sent as ServicePower's nlaFlag; Model and Serial editable and saved onto the ticket; Est. time field on one line

HR Paperworks staff checklist: "Add Employer Signature" on the Confidentiality & Non-Compete Agreement opens the signature window right there (it only switched to a tab on the same page and did nothing); new "Send to Employer" on rows awaiting HR review (DM with the sign link); the sign link page can now complete the Confidentiality & Non-Compete Agreement (printed name / title + signature, multi-page PDF re-rendered and confirmed)

Warning Form: Previous Warnings print oldest first (1. = the first warning, whatever order they were entered), on new forms and every existing form's preview; Sent Warning Forms get "Edit Warnings 1-3" (reason / date / issued by) and "Regenerate PDF", both re-rendering the PDF with the signatures already collected

Trainees become Regular on their Field Start day from the hourly server job (Central time), even when nobody opens the Training List; Ticket Attendance (desktop + mobile) groups technicians ignoring capitals / extra spaces, so "Chris carroll" and "Chris Carroll" are one row

Pre-Claim: Repair Category is ServicePower's own list (Minor on-site service ... Major stock merchandise service) and sends ServicePower's code (2-13) instead of the cut-off name; header shows miles, the warranty provider with a ServicePower HUB link, REDO (red, opens the original ticket) and Pre-Auth (red) - read-only lookup of the call on ServicePower's Call Auth (status, requested / authorized, approved by, reason), else the AHS Pre-Auth

Claim List: clickable Claim To company chips with counts in the toolbar (like Need Claim List) - pick one or more to show only those companies. Pre-Claim: SQT claims fill Repair Category "Minor on-site service" and Defect Code MECH when empty (still changeable). Pre-Auth: the Job Code goes in coreInfo.jobCode, where ServicePower returns it on an RFA

Claims - Pre-Auth: ServicePower Call Auth (Request for Authorization) filled in from the app - queue of PT-Need PreAuthorization tickets (or any ticket by number), form laid out like ServicePower's (request details, the required questions, per-company Job Code dropdown, labor / parts pre-filled from the ticket / mileage / travel with running total), Save Draft / Save as Ready, Managed by, Pending / Completed cards, date range, funnel filter on every column, preview of what would be sent. Sending is locked: Submit only sends when a SuperAdmin turns it on in Admin - Company Settings - ServicePower (off by default) and still asks before each one. Claims, Parts and BizOps roles plus Admin/SuperAdmin (migration 0401)

Pre-Claim job codes per company: GE (MA00 / MG00 / SS00 / SG00), SQT Repair / Job Code 1 (REP / BER / CNR / NPF / PNA), Assurant Job Code / Tier Code (MA00-MA04, T200-T403 with tier and note); Electrolux / Frigidaire shows the Defect Code in the Job Code spot (Pull from SP kept). Claim To account / claim company checked before manufacturer / brand. The box shows only the code, its description underneath

Expenses: Type of Reimbursement on Reimbursement Forms - Gas, Food or Other (specify), required on Self-Service and mobile, shown on the employee's list; Accounting Expenses gets a Type column (coloured pill) with a funnel filter (Gas / Food / Other / -) that also drives the cards and total (migration 0400)

Sent Warning Forms: counter of people by number of warnings (1st, 2nd, 3rd, more than 3 - signed or awaiting signatures, cancelled not counted); clicking a chip narrows the table and opens a centred popup listing those people (role, branch, warnings, pending, latest) - clicking a name shows only their forms

Expenses: only Accounting (plus Admin/SuperAdmin) can approve, reject or mark reimbursed - others see Awaiting Accounting; enforced in the database (migration 0393). Guides: BizOps Operations tile limited to BizOps roles plus Admin/SuperAdmin

Guides: BizOps Operations tile with three look-only tours from the Operations Guidelines - Working the OP queues (Ticket List), Checking parts shipments (Refresh for Marcone/Encompass, NSA and GE portal steps with Copy / Open), Need Cancel; tour steps can show a value with Copy and outside links

Claims: GE job code dropdown on Pre-Claim (label note beside it); Need Claim List red REDO pill, Claim To company colours and a colour key with clickable company chips; Claims Dashboard same company colours on the chart plus company chips (display only - nothing is sent to providers)

Pre-Claim: clicking a photo opens a zoomable side preview on the right (zoom, drag, rotate, prev/next) so the serial can be typed while reading it; ServicePower's Invalid manufacturerName/serviceCenterNumber shown as ServicePower account locked. Ticket page: REDO badge next to Claims Readiness (opens the original ticket)

Claim List: checkable Account filter (pick several) and a funnel filter on every column; Parts Done popup: per-day breakdown (Received by PO date, Collections by schedule date, Pickup today), only days with data

Expenses: Hotel and Car Rental tabs (Add Expense starts on that category), date range at the top driving the summary cards, total and list, and a funnel filter on every column (replaces the Employee/Category/Status/Month dropdowns)

Payroll adjustments: Tax as a % of gross pay (auto-calculated, 3 decimals) next to reimbursements/deductions - net pay, payslip, payroll run and Self-Service payslips (migration 0387). Time Correction: HR rejecting an approved correction only undoes the fields it changed, so a later punch (e.g. Time Out) is kept
Time Correction (desktop + mobile): picking a date pre-fills Check In, Check Out, Meal Start and Meal End from that day's timecard; change only what's wrong

Revert "Time Correction: Corrected Check In and Check Out are required again (desktop + mobile), meal start/end still required when the shift is over 6 hours"

This reverts commit 1fa2641cc46ead04172a8edc59463854ce6c5999.
Time Correction: Corrected Check In and Check Out are required again (desktop + mobile), meal start/end still required when the shift is over 6 hours

Payroll: Prev / Next employee in the payroll popup; Adjustments (reimbursements + / deductions -) per employee per pay period for PH payroll and US Office staff (Parts Manager, Parts Team Leader, Parts, Accounting, Admin-level) - net pay in the table (net green, gross muted), on the payslip PDF/emails, saved with Generate Payroll and shown on Self-Service payslips (migration 0386)

Payroll payslip emails: Email All Payslips for checked employees (skips $0 / no email, progress + summary) with a Send payslip emails? confirmation listing every recipient; checkbox per department; production email wording (test-email line removed); Finance/Admin/SuperAdmin can include their own row (migration 0385)

AHS Server Status: Uploads & signing papers section (real upload/download/remove test, signature-to-PDF image proxy check, signing activity, live upload test from the browser with server-side cleanup); per-person upload and signing error log (app_error_log, migration 0379) with Person / time-range dropdown

AHS Server Status module (SuperAdmin only): live checks of Supabase, Firebase, Cloudflare hosting, cron jobs, provider status pages and outside services, with uptime history from the 5-minute cron (Cloudflare judged only on Workers/DNS/SSL/CDN); Expenses: Hotel / Car Rental / Office Supply / Reimbursement Form categories, Month filter for the summary, Flash Tech expense lines take the trip's Hotel/Rental Rate (were stuck at $0) and show the trip's receipts

Schedule history for Time In/Out Required (effective-from date, past days judged by the schedule in force that day); required approval notes for Manager/HR/Accounting on PTO, Time Corrections and Ticket Time Disputes (shown in the Comments column); Accounting signs exception-report approvals like the Manager (comments + signature stamped in the PDF)

Flash Tech Travel & Expense Policy Agreement: company letterhead + watermark on every page, new "Ineligible Purchases and Reimbursement Limitations" section, "Financial Recovery & Legal Remedies" kept together on page 4, Regenerate PDF in HR Paperworks; shared letterhead helper (Performance Bonus Policy uses it too)
Performance Bonus Policy PDF: logo watermark drawn on top of the page content (faint, centered) — the new PDF's white page background was hiding it underneath
Performance Bonus Policy & Acknowledgment Form: updated PDF ("Full Disqualification" heading moved to page 2) — name, signature and date boxes moved down to the new signature lines

Performance Bonus Policy & Acknowledgment Form: new version (ranks C $100 / B $200 / A $400 / S $700 / SS $1,000; 50% reduction only for those appealing their plus one) — same layout and signature lines

Performance Bonus Policy PDF: company letterhead on every page (logo top-left, ribbon top-right, contact footer), faint logo watermark behind the text, form content at 92% so it fits between them; signature/name/date boxes moved to match
PTO / Sick / Unpaid Leave (desktop + mobile): Position is locked to the employee's primary role (read-only), filled in once their profile loads

Rest day history with "Effective from" (migration 0371): changing rest days no longer rewrites past months — Absent List, Attendance Status, Attendance Monitoring, employee calendar and absence alerts check the rest days in force on each date; user edit page gets Effective from + a Rest day history box. HR Hiring: All / Technician / US Staff / PH Staff filter for the pipeline and table.

Fix false absences: the shared timecard loader paged with a non-unique sort (work date only), so same-day rows could fall between pages and be skipped (48 of 3,669 in Sep 2026); now sorted by date, employee, id. Employee page loads only that employee's month.
Login Security: "Random password on Forgot Password" toggle — when on, Forgot Password emails a random 4-letter + 4-number temporary password instead of the default

Attendance starts on the hire / training start date: no absences, Missing or clock-in alerts before it (Absent List, Attendance Status "Not Started", Attendance Monitoring, alerts); HR Hiring "Not Created" asks for the start date and Add User requires it (saved as Master List Hire Date); SuperAdmin time edits stay CP
Exception Reports SL-UL: HR "Add Photo" button beside Reject when a request has no proof photo yet

Exception Reports: Finalize (final HR sign-off after Additional Review Required) and a Photos column on SL-UL; Sick/Unpaid Leave require a proof photo or PDF (desktop + mobile); Time Correction only for the same day or by the next weekday (Friday until Monday)
Attendance Status: Reset day button beside the pencil (HR/Admin) clears Time In, Meal and Time Out back to blank, with a Yes/No confirm

Time Out no longer looks dead: the pre-save trainee-review check asks "any trainees?" first (two tiny queries) and never holds a clock-out more than 8 s; the header clock shows "Saving..." right away and on-screen success/error messages instead of browser pop-ups
Messages: Mark as unread / Mark as read on each conversation in the header drop-down and the floating messenger (the other person's Seen is kept; migration 0365 message_reads.marked_unread)
Forgot Password: "Already have a code? Enter it" (also offered when the hourly code limit is hit); reset codes now last 24 hours

Default Password setting: Admin sets the company's default password in Login Security (set-only, never shown back); new accounts, Reset to default, Forgot Password and the Send Credentials email all use it (migration 0364 company_default_passwords)
Forgot Password: Unique ID picks the account (same as sign-in), and a 6-digit code emailed to the address on file must be entered before the password is reset (migration 0363 password_reset_codes)

Forgot Password: automatic reset to the default password, emailed from the IT Gmail to the address on file (username lookup shows the masked email / "Username doesn't exist"); default password now read from the DEFAULT_RESET_PASSWORD secret; Meetings Done: edit notes
Mobile Home: punches inside the hero, clock-in code in the hero corner, collapsible My Standing, blue/navy colour refinement; Time Off exception report for Personal/Sick/Unpaid
Mobile Home redesign: blue hero card, round punch buttons, round shortcuts

Chat: reactions, reply and forward from a ⋯ menu on each message

- Team Messenger page and the floating messenger: hover a message for ⋯ →
  quick reactions (👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏), Reply, Forward, Copy text
- Reactions show as chips (yours highlighted, hover for who) and update
  live; replies show the quoted original (click to jump); forwards are
  tagged "Forwarded from …" and keep the original author
- Migration 0360: message_reactions (own add/remove, on realtime) and
  message_links (reply / forward info for your own messages)

Messages: Sent / Delivered / Seen read receipts on direct messages

- Team Messenger page and the floating messenger show a check per message:
  Sent (saved), Delivered (they've had the app open since), Seen (they've
  opened the conversation since), with "Seen 3:25 PM" under your latest
- Conversation list shows the receipt before "You:" when the last message
  is yours
- Open conversations re-check every few seconds; the Messenger page now
  marks a thread read when a reply lands while it's open
- Uses existing message_reads + presence — no migration

Master List: download Excel / CSV of the rows shown

Exports the current tab, search and column filters with the same values
and order as the table (active first), plus Email; Branch on the Parts
tab and Tier Level on Current Technicians.
Home: logo silhouette watermark, centered behind the page

Announcements: titles, ticker with on/off; redesigned header drop-downs, Notification Center and Team Messenger

- Announcements page rebuilt: titles, filters, search, unread, composer
- Ticker under the header shows announcement titles, starts from the right;
  Activate / Deactivate per line, On / Off for the whole ticker, Remove kept
  on record (migration 0355: announcement_marquees, announcement_titles,
  announcement_marquee_settings, set_ticker_enabled)
- Local-only preview samples (dev builds only, never saved)
- Header drop-downs share one design: day groups, type icons, avatars,
  unread rows, short times, links shortened
- Notification Center and Team Messenger restyled (chat bubbles, day
  dividers, full-height layout)

Module pages + page breadcrumb with icons; "waiting on you" badges everywhere

- Shared attention counts (src/lib/attention.ts, cached a minute) behind
  Home's attention strip, module/page card badges, the breadcrumb strip and
  tab badges (Attendance Monitoring PTO / Corrections / Ticket Dispute;
  Employee Monitoring PTO Management / Exceeded / Time Corrections;
  Paid / Unpaid Leave buttons)
- Module landing pages: icon tile in the module colour, accent page cards
- Breadcrumb strip above every page: Home › Module › Page
- Styles for all of the above, the announcements page, ticker, header
  drop-downs, Notification Center, Team Messenger and app-wide scrollbars

Home "Today" + module cards; Time Off Calendar range + frozen header; Exceeded leave columns

- Home: greeting with date and a compact "Needs your attention" strip —
  managers see what's assigned to them to approve (PTO/leave, sick leave,
  time corrections, ticket disputes); HR/Admin see company-wide pending PTO,
  corrections and over-limit; everyone sees unread notifications/messages;
  Parts gets "click DONE". Module cards get icons, accent colours, badges,
  and sub-links that open their own page.
- Time Off Calendar: manual From/To date range; date header stays frozen
  while scrolling.
- Exceeded -> Time Corrections: From/To range (limit = 2 per month in the
  range); V/S/P/H/U/B/A leave columns, clickable for details; A = Unnoticed
  (marked, or pending/rejected leave) + Absent (missed workday, nothing filed).

UI kit: standard buttons, dropdowns, popup, toasts, loading rows, empty states; mobile buttons

- .btn / .btn-primary / .btn-danger / .btn-ghost / .btn-sm and .ui-select,
  light and dark
- AppModal (one popup frame), AppToaster (toasts now actually show),
  EmptyState, TableSkeleton
- Reduced-motion support
- Mobile: primary buttons use the app's primary colour, 44px touch targets,
  focus rings; green kept for Clock In / Work Start / Approve
- Piloted on Part Daily Collection and the Parts Done button/banner

Training List: match hiring records to accounts by phone or email

A trainee account with no phone number showed twice (once from Hiring,
once from Master List). Current Trainee, Field Starts, auto-graduation,
Quit/Stopped account deactivation and daily punches now link a hiring
record to its account by phone or email.

Ticket Guides: each department only sees its own tour

- CSR tour for CSR roles, Triage for Technical Support, Parts for Parts /
  Parts Team Leader / Parts Manager / Parts Order, Claims (coming) for
  Claims roles; Admin and Super Admin see all
- Applies to Guides -> Ticket Guides (only your tabs, message if none) and
  the ticket page's Tour menu (hidden when you have no tour)

Parts: brand picker + Make/MFG on orders, Part Info on every row, Done on each Parts page, aging from delivered date

- Part Transaction: magnifying-glass Part Info on every part row; Brand
  dropdown under Part Dist. for Marcone/Encompass listing each brand with
  stock, saved on the part (parts.dist_brand, migration 0348; saving is
  safe before the migration)
- Submit PO popup: title per distributor, Make (Marcone) / MFG (Encompass)

- Done button (shared component) on Part Receive, Part Daily Pickup and

- Part Receive: Aging counts business days from the Delivered Date (to the

Approving Requests guide: tour of Attendance Monitoring for managers and above

- Guides -> Approving Requests (and a Tour button on Attendance Monitoring):
  alerts and clocking a technician in from Missing Clock In, Time-Off

Guides module with guided tours (desktop + mobile), eBay Excel import

- Guides module: Getting Started (header + home), Ticket Guides (CSR,
  Triage, Parts tours of the ticket page; Claims coming), Self-Service Guide

Company clock-in code for Time In, top-level clock-in at every branch, trainee flags and punches

- Clock-In Codes (HR and Branch/Technician tiles): one 4-digit company code per
  day; technicians and branch leaders (Technician, Technician Manager, Branch
  Manager, SBM, TD, TAD — primary or extra role, not PH) enter it to Time In on

- Approval Chain top level can clock in technicians at every branch (mobile

- Trainees: Clock In Team / Team Attendance read and write the trainee

- View as on mobile now includes Parts, Parts Manager, Parts Team Leader
- Migrations 0340-0342, 0344-0347

Part Daily Collection rework, HR notes in daily summaries, pickup reset on status revert

- Part Daily Collection: Collect column first and pinned, merged Part/Ticket/Dates
  columns, Not collected / Collected / All switch with counts, auto-filled
  Used/Restock qty, sticky Save bar with unsaved count + Discard, edits kept

- Part Daily Pickup: removed example rows; unticking clears picked_up_date
- Migration 0336: clear picked_up when a part's status goes back to

Performance: Ticket List and HR Dashboard Hiring tab were both loading/rendering far more than needed.

Ticket List: scope the default fetch to the last 6 months (with a "Load full history" link, auto-upgrading if an older Start Date is picked) instead of the company's entire ticket history; cap "All" page size at 1000 rendered rows; debounce the search box before the expensive per-column filter-option recompute; precompute per-ticket status-log/visited-by lookups instead of rescanning per row per render; session-only cache for an instant repeat-visit paint. getCompanyTickets() itself is unchanged for every other caller (Operations/Claims/CSR dashboards, KPI pages) — scoping is opt-in and local to this page.

HR Dashboard Hiring tab: paginate the candidate table at 50/page — live-measured this was rendering all 626 rows unpaginated (~70k DOM nodes, ~8s of blocked main-thread time during a scroll), confirmed via a live authenticated test; after the fix, 5,919 DOM nodes and no sustained blocking. Debounce the company-wide "someone edited a candidate" realtime reload (800ms) instead of a full reload per single change; switch branch manager/assigned interviewer/manager/trainer lookups from a per-row array scan to a precomputed map; stagger other tabs' (Warnings/PTO/Attendance/Manager Requests) initial loads a beat later instead of competing with Hiring's own; same session-cache pattern for the candidate list.

Consolidated MessagesMenu + FloatingMessenger onto one shared realtime subscription (realtimeMessagesBus.ts) instead of each opening its own duplicate channel; trimmed the header's 800ms refresh debounce to 250ms.

Messaging: chat messages now render through the shared MessageBody component (markdown-style [label](url) links, plain URLs, #ticket refs) instead of raw text, fixing unclickable/overflowing signed-document notification links in the floating messenger. Every "document signed" notification's link now also carries a companion "View in Staff Checklist" link that deep-links straight to that employee's row via a URL hash, parsed from the existing filename label — no changes needed across the 20+ individual form pages that send these notifications.
(cherry picked from commit 669fe05f2f087365d771ed9761cb76d527a76a97)

Reduce sustained Supabase load: dedupe/scope MessagesMenu notifications, cheap-peek 3 more pollers

MessagesMenu's realtime subscription and poll each independently decided
whether to play the notification sound with no shared memory between
them, so every message played it twice (once via realtime, once again on
the next poll tick). Worse, neither path checked whether a DM was
actually the current user's — any DM between two OTHER coworkers in the
company rang the bell and fired a refresh for everyone else too. Both
paths now share a "have I already notified for this message" guard and
skip DM messages the user isn't a participant in.

Also extended the cheap-peek pattern (already applied to
AnnouncementBanner/MessagesMenu's poll) to three more pollers that were
still doing a full unconditional refetch every tick alongside their own
realtime subscription:
- LiveChatSupportPage.tsx: session-list poll (5s) and active-thread poll
  (4s) — the latter's full getLiveChatMessages() call also writes
  delivered_at/read_at every time, so this cuts an unconditional write
  down to only ticks where something's actually new.
- MobileTechApp.tsx: 5s DM thread poll.

New shared peek helpers: peekLiveChatSessionsSignature/
peekLatestLiveChatMessageId (liveChat.ts), peekLatestThreadMessage
(messaging.ts).

Left LiveChatWidget.tsx's poll alone — investigated it too, but its
messages aren't append-only (delivered_at/read_at mutate on existing
rows to drive read-receipt checkmarks), so the same peek-and-skip
optimization risks breaking those checkmarks without a bigger
server-side redesign. Not worth the regression for the lowest-priority
poller of the four.

Fix race condition that prevented logging back in after a session-lock kickout

A kickout's firebaseSignOut() is async, so its delayed "signed out"
notification could land after a fresh login on the same device, or a
stray duplicate auth event could race the real login's session claim
before it finished writing — either way, the device would immediately
sign itself back out right after a successful re-login.

- Coalesce concurrent session checks per Firebase uid so a duplicate
  event reuses the real login's in-flight result instead of comparing
  against not-yet-committed data.
- Ignore a stale "signed out" notification if Firebase's own current
  user shows someone is already signed in again by the time it arrives.
- Add a generation guard so an older auth event can't clobber state a
  newer one already established.

Fix stray colon artifact in Jotform values, surface attachment failures, add submission delete

- Some Jotform field types (Full Name, Textarea, Date, Signature) prefix
  their rawRequest value with a stray leading colon, which was breaking
  the "starts with uploads/" file-detection check and any bare-filename
  reconstruction relying on it as a sibling path. Now stripped before any
  file-shape check or display.
- mirrorSubmissionFiles now returns per-file error summaries alongside
  successful uploads, stored as a new attachmentErrors field so a failed
  attachment is visible in the submission modal instead of only a server
  log nobody watches in production.
- Added deleteNotification() and a delete button beside each Jotform
  submission's timestamp in the list.

Fix Jotform answer/attachment parsing: metadata leaking, signature shapes, real question titles

- Filter Jotform's own submission bookkeeping (slug, jsExecutionTracker,
  submitSource/Date, buildDate, uploadServerUrl) out of the answer list —
  only real qN_-keyed question answers should show.
- Recognize signatures/uploads in every shape Jotform sends: full URL,
  bare "uploads/..." path, bare filename (resolved via a sibling file's
  path prefix in the same submission), and inline base64 data URIs
  (Jotform's signature "Type" mode, as opposed to "Draw" mode's uploaded
  file).
- Pull real question titles from Jotform's Form API instead of guessing
  from the internal field key, since copy-pasting a field in Jotform's
  builder keeps the original internal name even after the displayed
  question text is edited. Falls back to the old heuristic if the API
  call fails. Duplicate titles (fields that genuinely share identical
  text in the form itself) get auto-numbered so they stay distinguishable.

Fix /api/jotform 404 in production: route was never wired into the Worker

src/server.ts special-cases supabase-token/servicepower/marcone before
falling through to the page router, but jotform was missing from that
list — so any request to /api/jotform in the deployed Worker fell
through to the SPA router and got a 404 + homepage HTML instead of
reaching the webhook handler. Local testing never caught this because
the dev-only jotformDevPlugin in vite.config.ts mounts the same route
via Vite middleware, masking the gap.

Fix "View as [Role]" preview not carrying over to a new tab, letting restricted content open via right-click

Reported as: right-clicking a submodule to open it in a new tab could
still open it even though it should have been restricted. Traced this
to the "View as" role-preview feature (Super Admin only) rather than a
real access-control gap — every tile grid (home.tsx, ModuleNavigator.tsx,
m.$module.tsx) already correctly hides a restricted submodule via
canAccessSubmodule, which deliberately mirrors the destination route's
own enforcement in m.$module.$submodule.tsx.

The actual bug: viewAsRoleState was persisted to sessionStorage, which
is scoped per-tab. Right-clicking a tile to open it in a new tab (or
middle-click, Ctrl+click) opens a browser tab with its own empty
sessionStorage, so the preview never carried over — the new tab silently
fell back to the Super Admin's own real, unrestricted access, making it
look like the restriction was bypassed. A real restricted-role user
isn't affected by this at all (their role comes from the Firebase/
Supabase session, which does persist across tabs); this only ever
applied to a Super Admin using the preview to test what a role can see.

Switched all 4 call sites (initial read, setViewAsRole's write/clear,
the stale-preview cleanup effect, and logout's cleanup — the last of
these had already drifted to sessionStorage while the others had not,
which would have left a stale preview in localStorage after logout once
the others were fixed) to localStorage, so the preview is shared across
every open tab. The existing stale-value safety net (clearing the
preview the moment a signed-in account turns out not to be a Super
Admin) and the always-visible "still previewing" banner both still work
unchanged — neither depends on which storage mechanism is used.

Verified via tsc, a full two-stage build, and a local wrangler dev smoke
test (/, /landing, /home — all 200, zero server errors).

Fix the <Navigate> infinite-loop fix: caused a full production outage

The previous fix (React.memo-wrapped Navigate, later a useNavigate()+
useEffect replacement) re-imported Navigate from a wrapper module instead
of straight from @tanstack/react-router. Deployed, it took production
down entirely: every single request — every route, every static asset —
started throwing "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined
(reading 'extends')" from the router's own SSR route-tree/dehydrate step
(confirmed live via wrangler tail on adminhubsolution.com, then
reproduced locally with `wrangler dev` against the built dist output).
Rolled back to the pre-deploy version to restore service, then bisected
locally (checking out each of the last 4 commits and running the built
Worker) to confirm it was this change, then bisected file-by-file within
it to confirm it's specifically the import source — @tanstack/start's
route file analysis needs `Navigate` imported directly (unaliased) from
"@tanstack/react-router" in a route file to build its route manifest
correctly.

New approach: leave every `import { ..., Navigate, ... } from
"@tanstack/react-router"` untouched, and instead guard how many times
each call site is ALLOWED to render a fresh <Navigate> with
useRedirectGuard() (src/lib/useRedirectGuard.ts) — a ref keyed on the
target's own to/replace fields. The first render for a given target
renders the real <Navigate> once (firing navigate() via its own effect,
unchanged); every subsequent render with the SAME target renders null
instead of a new <Navigate> props object, so navigate() never re-fires
and the loop can't start — while a render with a different target still
fires normally.

Verified: local `wrangler dev` on the built dist output returns 200 for
/, /landing, /home, /announcements, /tickets/map, and
/m/report/report-technician-performance (previously 500 on literally
every route). Re-ran the original Playwright infinite-loop repro
(hr.testing, a TECHNICIAN-role account, hitting a page it's denied
access to) against the same build: 0 "Maximum update depth exceeded"
errors, same as the first fix. tsc and both build stages pass.

Fix infinite render loop / React "hasn't mounted yet" warning from <Navigate> in render

@tanstack/react-router's <Navigate> decides whether to fire navigate() by
comparing its whole props object by reference; JSX like
<Navigate to="/home" replace /> builds a fresh object every render, so any
re-render of the component returning it re-fires navigate(), which changes
router state, which re-renders it again. With an access-gate redirect whose
condition never resolves (e.g. a role denied a page) this spins forever
("Maximum update depth exceeded" — reproduced live on
/m/report/report-technician-performance as a TECHNICIAN-role account);
otherwise it just double-fires during mount, which is the React "state
update on a component that hasn't mounted yet" warning.

AccountPageShell.tsx, announcements.tsx) via a same-name import alias, so
no call sites needed touching. Verified live via Playwright: the same

Fix deploy failure caused by exceljs resolving its Node entry for SSR

exceljs's package.json "main" points at a Node-targeted entry
(excel.js -> lib/exceljs.nodejs.js, pulling in archiver/unzipper/etc.
along the way) rather than its browser-safe "browser" field
(dist/exceljs.min.js). Vite's client build picks up "browser"
automatically; the SSR/Workers build resolved "main" instead, like a
real Node host — except Cloudflare Workers isn't Node, so that entry's
own top-level code (assumes real Node globals) crashed the Worker
script at `wrangler deploy` validation time ("Cannot set properties of
undefined (setting 'base64')"), before the client-only handler that's
its one actual caller could ever run.

Aliases `exceljs` straight to its own browser bundle for every
environment, sidestepping the main/browser field split entirely, and
drops the now-dead manualChunks entries for its Node-only dependencies
(no longer resolved into the graph at all with the alias in place).

responsive display scale, so any container resize (fires almost
immediately on a narrow/mobile screen) re-triggered the whole pdf.js
load+render from scratch, racing a second render against the first on
the same canvas with only one easily-outrun cancellation check -
occasionally leaving the canvas blank while the overlay inputs still
rendered on top of it. Render is now done once per document load at a
fixed pixel density, decoupled from the responsive scale (CSS handles
the resize), and a failed render now shows a visible error with a

typed/pasted by a user, confirmed reproducible) makes

abort the whole PDF fill. Added a shared sanitizeForFont() helper and
wired it into all 16 *PdfFill.ts scripts so one unsupported character

document: Angelo Mendoza's Master PH Contractor Agreement showed

Paperworks → Sent Termination Forms panel (has to run from a real
browser — the capture pipeline needs html2canvas/DOM, not something a
backend script can do). Meant to be run once and then removed along
with this button once confirmed there's nothing left to fix.

Fix multi-signer PDFs missing all but the last signature A termination form (or promotion form, warning form, manager's action plan form — any signable document with more than one signature slot) signed by 2-3 people in sequence showed every signature fine in the live in-app preview (plain tags need no CORS), but the actual exported/downloaded PDF only ever had the LAST signer's — every earlier signer's line came out blank. Root cause: each sign page's PDF-capture step only swapped the signer's OWN slot to a local data: URL before calling captureHtmlToPdfBlob (html2canvas can't read pixels from a cross-origin firebasestorage.googleapis.com URL without CORS, so it silently skips whatever it can't load). Every OTHER slot signed at an earlier stage was still left as a real Firebase Storage URL, which worked fine the first time (nothing else to composite yet) but broke as soon as a second or third signer's turn came and the PDF got regenerated with everyone's signatures at once. New resolveSignaturesForCapture() in pdfCapture.ts fetches every earlier signature and converts it to its own local data: URL too (best-effort — a slot whose fetch fails just keeps its original URL), so the whole composited image is 100% local by the time html2canvas runs. Wired into all 8 affected sign pages (internal + external variants of warning/promotion/action-plan/termination forms) — the only document types with more than one signature slot chained sequentially; the master-agreement flows (ManagerReviewPage.tsx) already store the employee's signature as a raw data: URL directly in form_data rather than a Storage URL, so they were never affected. Note: this only fixes documents signed FROM NOW ON — a document that already finished signing under the old bug (its stored pdf_url) still has the blank signature lines baked into that PDF and needs a manual re-generation if the historical record needs correcting.

used as a rare fallback — reliably forces a real download and never
opens a tab; opening a tab is now only the true fallback, when the
fetch itself fails (e.g. a CORS gap), with a visible alert if even
that gets popup-blocked instead of failing silently. This fixes the
same "opens a tab instead of downloading" behavior everywhere in the

CSR overtime: flat 40 hrs/week instead of the scheduled-duty-hours cap

CSR shift start/end times vary person to person and aren't reliably captured
in required_check_in/required_check_out, so the weekly-reset overtime cap
(splitRegularOvertimeWeekly, capped at each week's own scheduled duty hours)
doesn't apply cleanly to them - a missing or stale schedule field would
silently misclassify their overtime. CSR now uses a flat 40 hrs/week
threshold instead (standard FLSA overtime), which doesn't depend on
per-person schedule data being accurate at all.

- timecards.ts: splitRegularOvertimeWeekly takes an optional
  flatWeeklyThreshold param that overrides the schedule-derived weekly cap;
  new CSR_WEEKLY_OVERTIME_THRESHOLD = 40 constant.

  isCsrRestrictedRole(role, extraRoles) routes CSR through the flat
  threshold instead of computeScheduledDutyHours.

  added role/extraRoles props (threaded through from both callers above)
  since the modal didn't previously receive role at all.

shown alongside Total Hours - not what actually splits regular/overtime)
deliberately stays schedule-derived for CSR: it's a whole-period total, and

longer than one week.

Fix "Download PDF" silently doing nothing on origins Firebase Storage's CORS config doesn't cover

Root cause of "some files aren't showing" — confirmed live from real console
errors fetching real substance-screening PDFs from a LAN dev-server origin:
every one of the 28 "Download PDF" buttons in ReportHRDaily.tsx fetch()ed the
file to rename it via a blob, which requires Storage's CORS config to
include the exact origin the app is viewed from. When it doesn't, the fetch
throws — and the fallback (window.open() from inside that async catch
block) runs after the click's synchronous "user gesture" window has closed,
so browsers silently popup-block it too. Net effect: nothing happens at
all, no visible error, and the download just doesn't work — no signature,
no PDF, nothing.

New shared downloadSignableDocumentPdf() opens a blank tab SYNCHRONOUSLY
before the fetch (still inside the gesture, never blocked), then redirects
that tab to the renamed blob if the fetch succeeds or the raw URL if it
doesn't — degrading to "just open the file" instead of downloading nothing.
Replaced all 28 duplicated fetch/blob/catch blocks with calls to it
(scripted replacement, verified 1:1 against the originals).

Fix Technician Form Checklist: completed two-party forms showed as "Not sent"

Root cause: recipientId isn't a stable "whose form is this" identity — it's
"who currently needs to act." Every employer/HR-countersign form (wage_ack,
damage, i9, meal_rest_break, mileage_fuel, parts_responsibility,
substance_screening, location_consent, flash_technician_travel)
reassigns recipientId to whichever HR staffer completes the review step
(reassignSignableDocument in each "*EmployerDialog" handler), permanently
severing the link to the original technician the moment the form is
actually finished. The checklist grouped documents by recipientId, so a
fully confirmed form vanished back to "Not sent" as soon as HR completed
it — confirmed against production: 212 real (technician, form type)
completions across the company were invisible this way, each one also
incorrectly counted as incomplete for auto-unfreeze eligibility.

formData.employeeId is set once at document creation by every send handler
and never changes — it's the real stable identity. TechnicianFormChecklistPage
now groups by formData.employeeId (falling back to recipientId only if
that's somehow unset), and getSignableDocumentsForRecipient (which backs
getIncompleteTechnicianForms / the frozen-account "what do I still need to
sign" popup — both hit the same bug) now matches on recipient_id OR
form_data->>employeeId instead of recipient_id alone.

Fix mobile ticket scoping regression: managers with a TECHNICIAN extra role saw no tickets

Fix PDF fill/sign pages stuck on "Loading form…" on older browsers

pdfjs-dist 6.x calls Promise.try internally (its main bundle and worker
bundle both do), a method only shipped in browsers from late 2024+. On an
older browser it throws, the worker falls back to "fake worker" mode, and
the same missing method throws again on the main thread — leaving every
real-PDF fill/sign page (mileage & fuel policy, wage ack, I-9, etc.) stuck
loading forever. Reported by a technician (Matt Simmons) whose mileage
policy form never loaded past the spinner.

Polyfilling Promise.try at the root route, before any pdfjs-dist import can
run, fixes every one of these pages at once instead of patching each.

Warn before resending an HR form that's already on file

Traced the hr_signable_documents duplicate rows (some recipients had 40-100+
copies of the same form) to two sources: two HR accounts repeatedly
self-testing the send flow (409 rows, deleted from production), and the
Bulk Form Send / individual Send buttons having no idea a form was already
sent — one new hire got the same 5-document onboarding packet twice, 16
minutes apart, same person, no warning either time.

Every Send handler for a bulk-sendable form type now checks for an existing
non-cancelled document for that recipient first and confirms before sending
again, instead of silently creating another row.

Added pickAuthoritativeDocument (signableDocumentRegistry.ts):

Verified against production: found 19 real recipient+type combos

Also surfaced, while investigating, a much bigger and separate issue:

Fix Team Messenger's 2s poll — was the #1 query by total time in prod

Supabase's own Query Performance report (Total Time > 1000ms filter)
showed a "messages.id, sender_id, ..." query as the single biggest
time sink in the whole project — 29.3% of total time, 68,338 calls,
37ms mean. Traced it to TeamMessenger.tsx's realtime fallback poll:
every 2 seconds, for as long as any thread is open, it ran the FULL
getChannelMessages/getDmMessages (up to 200 rows, every column) —
despite its own comment claiming this was "cheap, one indexed query".

AnnouncementBanner.tsx and MessagesMenu.tsx already use for their own
fallback polls: peekLatestThreadMessage (a single-row id/timestamp
check) runs every 2s as before, and the expensive full fetch only
fires on the tick something actually changed. Keeps the same 2s
fallback responsiveness, cuts the cost of nearly every tick to a
single indexed row read instead of up to 200 full rows.

Widen the two app-wide realtime fallback polls to cut background DB load

AnnouncementBanner.tsx (4s) and MessagesMenu.tsx (8s) both poll the
messages table as a fallback behind their real Supabase Realtime
subscription — both are mounted for EVERY logged-in user on EVERY
page all day. Widened both to 20s: realtime is still the instant fast
path in the normal case, this fallback only matters when realtime is
actually down, where a 20s worst-case delay instead of 4-8s is an
easy trade for meaningfully less continuous background query volume
company-wide.

Investigated in response to a Supabase dashboard RAM usage question —
no connection leaks found (no raw Postgres connections anywhere in
the app; every realtime subscription's cleanup is already correctly
wired), and actual table sizes are small (thousands of rows, not
enough to explain memory pressure on their own). These two polls were
the clearest concrete, safe, reversible lever available at the
application level.

Remove geofence auto-clock-out — was firing on the first GPS fix, not a return

TechnicianLocationTracker.tsx auto-clocked a technician out (unreviewed,
if within 0.5mi of their home address) or queued a reviewed checkout
proposal (if within 1mi of their branch) the moment ANY GPS fix landed
inside that radius — with no check that they'd ever left it first.
Anyone whose home is near the office, or who simply clocks in from the
branch parking lot (normal), got auto-clocked-out within moments of
starting their shift. From a technician's perspective this looked
exactly like getting kicked out, even though it was never an auth
session issue — it was writing a real timecard check_out.

Removed the whole geofence check (branch/home coordinate resolution,
the haversine distance check, and the auto-checkout/proposal calls)
per the user's explicit call to just remove the radius rather than add
a "has left the radius yet" guard. The end-of-day fallback for a
forgotten Time Out (technicianForcedCheckout.ts, server-side at 11:59
PM local) is untouched and still covers that case. mapEngine.ts's
radius constants and technicianCheckoutProposals.ts's create/approve
functions are left in place (unused now, but the Attendance
Monitoring review UI may still show historical proposal rows) rather
than deleted, to keep this change scoped to the actual trigger.

Close the "self-edit any column" gap on profiles

profiles_update's self-edit clause (firebase_uid = jwt sub) had no
column restriction — RLS is row-level only, so any logged-in user
could PATCH their own role, extra_roles, is_active, frozen,
branch_access, employment_type, company_id, etc. via a raw REST call,
none of which the UI ever exposes to a non-admin self-edit.

Added a BEFORE UPDATE trigger (not a column GRANT/REVOKE, which isn't
row-aware and would also break ADMIN/HR/FINANCE editing someone
ELSE'S role/is_active/etc, which stays fully untouched here) that
applies restriction only when a user is editing their OWN row:

- role, schedule fields, and timezone stay self-editable exactly when
  profile.tsx's own UI already allows it (ADMIN/SUPERADMIN/
  SUPERSUPERADMIN for role; manager-tier+ for schedule; SUPERADMIN for
  timezone) - mirrored 1:1 from ACCOUNT_FIELD_EDIT_ROLES/
  SCHEDULE_EDIT_ROLES/canEditTimezone so this becomes real enforcement
  of the same rule the UI already claims to have, not a new one.
- must_change_password self-clear (password change flow) and frozen
  true->false (auto-unfreeze on form completion) are allowed in that
  one direction only; the reverse of either has no legitimate case.
- display_name, email, phone_number, department, assigned_branch,
  po_initials, working_hours, meal_minutes, and low-stakes contact/
  notification metadata stay unrestricted (confirmed real self-edit
  paths, none of it access-control-relevant).
- Everything else (extra_roles, is_active, company_id, branch_access,
  employment_type, manager_name, payroll_excluded, technician_id,
  username, employee_info, and every login-security/audit column) is
  blocked outright on self-edit - no legitimate self-edit call site
  exists for any of them anywhere in the app today.

Audited every self-edit call site in profile.tsx and users.ts's

Work Map: bulk-fetch cached geocodes instead of one throttled lookup per ticket

throttle -- so even addresses already geocoded still paid a serialized
network round-trip each, which was the actual bottleneck behind the
new "Loading tickets…" pill taking so long on a normal day where most
addresses are already known.

New bulkLookupGeocode() (geocodeCache.ts) resolves many addresses in
one batched query (200/batch, 5 batches concurrent, mirrors the
runBatched pattern from the ticket-id bulk lookups) instead of one
round-trip per address. warmGeocodeCache() (mapEngine.ts) uses it to
pre-populate the in-memory geocode cache before the per-ticket
geocode() loop runs, so cache hits resolve synchronously with zero
network calls -- genuine misses still fall through to geocode()'s
normal throttled live-provider path unchanged.

Verified against real data: 15/15 sample Chattanooga ticket addresses
resolved from geocode_cache in a single batched query.

Extracted buildTicketGeocodeQuery() so the pre-warm pass and the
actual per-ticket geocode call build the exact same query string --

Work Map: fix stale-map crash when a filter changes before office-zoom geocoding resolves

Found via a real crash: "Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties
of undefined (reading '_leaflet_pos')" in Leaflet's DomUtil, thrown
from setView() being called on a map instance whose underlying DOM
had already been torn down.

Root cause: when a selected location has zero geocodable tickets, the
effect falls back to geocoding the branch office and centering the
map on it. That callback checked `!position || !activeMap` but was
missing the `cancelled` check its sibling callback (the actual office
PIN marker, a few lines up) already had -- so if the date/location/
ticket-list changed again before this office geocode resolved, it
still tried to reposition a map that a newer effect run had already
replaced/torn down.

This bug predates the recent geocode concurrency cap, but that change
makes every geocode call (including this one) take meaningfully
longer under load, which widens the window for the race and makes it
far more likely to actually fire in practice.

Cap concurrent geocode() calls to stop ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES on large ticket lists

Work Map and Work Planner both throw a single Promise.all over every
visible ticket's address to place map pins -- fine for a handful of
tickets, but a location/day with a couple thousand (confirmed in a
real error trace: Promise.all index 2704) fires that many concurrent
geocode() calls in one shot. That's past what the browser can even
track (net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES) and floods Geoapify/Google
well past their rate limits, which then cascades into "Failed to
fetch" on requests that should have succeeded.

concurrency slots before doing any real work (DB cache lookup or live
provider call) and releases it after -- a true global cap since it's
module-level, not per-geocoder-instance. Every caller (Work Map, Work
Planner, anywhere else that calls makeGeocoder()) is protected
automatically; no call site needs to batch its own Promise.all.

bypassing the queue entirely.

Stop geocodeCache spamming warnings when crypto.subtle is unavailable

crypto.subtle only exists in a secure context (HTTPS, or the
special-cased localhost/127.0.0.1) -- it's undefined when reaching the
dev server over plain http:// from another device on the LAN (e.g.
http://192.168.x.x:8080), which is a normal way to test the mobile
view but not something the code accounted for. Every geocode lookup/
store call threw the same "Cannot read properties of undefined
(reading 'digest')" and got caught+logged individually, producing
dozens of near-duplicate console warnings.

now it's skipped up front with one warning per session instead of
throwing+catching per address. No change to production behavior --
Cloudflare Workers deployments are always HTTPS, so crypto.subtle is
always available there.

ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR on Work Planner, not general network flakiness.

report) silently rendered zero tickets instead of just being briefly
slower. This is what made ticket 1008117358-10 (and every other
ticket) appear to vanish from Work Planner -- not a filtering bug,

every ping upsert failed silently. The technician's own UI looked
fine (badge showing, no visible error) while their live location
never actually reached the database -- from a dispatcher's
perspective on Technician Whereabouts, that person's location just
never showed up.

timestamp field.

Cache getCompanyUsers and slow MessagesMenu's fallback poll, per pg_stat_statements

Pulled the actual Query Performance report (pg_stat_statements ordered by
total_exec_time) to find what's really driving the project's CPU/RAM
exhaustion, beyond the polling fix already made. Findings:

- getCompanyUsers() — a 5-query roster fetch (deliberately split so a
  missing migration column on one slice can't null out the others) — is
  called from 53 different files with no caching between them. Across its
  constituent queries this was ~28.5% of all database time. Wrapped it in a
  30s shared cache with in-flight dedup, so simultaneous callers on one page
  load share a single fetch and repeat calls within the window are free.
  Wired invalidateCompanyUsersCache() into createCompanyUser,
  createSupabaseAdminProfile, deleteCompanyUser, and updateCompanyUser so an
  admin's own edit is never hidden behind a stale cache.

- MessagesMenu's "did anything new arrive" fallback poll was 15% of total
  database time on its own (16,263 calls) despite each call being cheap —
  its own comment already said "polling every 8s" while the code said
  4000ms, same drift AnnouncementBanner had. Realtime is the documented fast
  path here; the poll is just the safety net for when realtime is off.
  Restored the interval to match what the comment always claimed.

Replace messages' channel/dm indexes with partial, company_id-leading ones

idx_messages_channel(channel_id, created_at) and idx_messages_dm(dm_thread_id,
created_at) from 0001_init.sql cover the same access pattern every
channel/DM-scoped message read already narrows to further: every such query
in messaging.ts filters deleted_at is null, and RLS (messages_select) always
adds company_id = auth_company_id() on top. A partial index scoped to
deleted_at is null, with company_id leading, lets Postgres satisfy both
predicates from one smaller index instead of an index scan plus a per-row
recheck — and stays smaller, so it's more likely to stay resident in
shared_buffers under the memory pressure the project's been under.

Four separate migration files because CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY can't
run inside a transaction block, and Supabase's SQL Editor wraps multiple
pasted statements in one implicit transaction — each has to be its own
standalone Run. 0194/0195 build the new indexes without blocking writes to
messages; 0196/0197 drop the old ones only after confirming the
replacements exist, so read queries are never left without a covering index
mid-migration.

Reduce sustained Supabase load: cheap-peek AnnouncementBanner poll, parallelize token bridge

The project's compute was pegged (CPU 71-94%, RAM 65-75% on a t4g.micro,
Supabase flagging active resource exhaustion). AnnouncementBanner.tsx's
fallback poll was doing a real message_reads write + messages read every 4s
unconditionally, in every open tab of every logged-in user, all day —
MessagesMenu.tsx's own equivalent poll already avoided this by peeking at
one cheap indexed row first and only paying for the full refresh when it
actually changed. Gave AnnouncementBanner the same shape: peek at the
channel's latest message id (already covered by idx_messages_channel) every
tick, only run refreshLastRead + getChannelMessages when that id moves.
Both components' own comments claimed "polling every 8s" while the code
said 4000ms in both — left the interval as-is since realtime is the fast
path and this is just the safety net, but worth noting the drift.

Also parallelized /api/supabase-token's recordLoginEvent + mintOrReadSessionId
calls (independent of each other, previously awaited back-to-back) — this
endpoint runs on every login, 45-min heartbeat, tab-focus, and page-load
restore, across every open tab. Added a composite index on
login_events(company_id, created_at desc) so the shared-IP anomaly check's
500-row company scan doesn't need a separate in-memory sort as the table
grows.

Fix ServicePower RFA error-message extraction (wrong shape, was hiding the real message)

The generic error boilerplate shared across ServicePower's own
integration guides shows a lowercase messages: [{ message }] shape, but
the RFA-retrieve endpoint's actual Response Elements table — confirmed
against the real live response — returns capitalized
Messages: [{ messageText }] instead. The previous code only checked
the lowercase shape, so real API errors silently fell through to a
generic "ServicePower returned an error" instead of showing what
ServicePower actually said.

This wasn't cosmetic: with the fix in place, the real message turned
out to be "Your User ID or Password is invalid. User ID will be
disabled after 2 more invalid attempts." — a near-lockout warning that
was completely invisible before. Also defensively handle Requests/
ResponseCode/MoreCallsExist capitalization on the success path, since
the same casing inconsistency could plausibly extend there too and it
hasn't been observed live yet (auth has never succeeded).

pattern already used on the ticket detail page (sticky top-[64px]).

A single <table> can't do this: putting position: sticky headers
inside an overflow-x-auto wrapper still traps them (CSS forces
overflow-y to auto the instant overflow-x isn't visible, so the
wrapper becomes the "nearest scrolling ancestor" sticky resolves
against, not the page). Split into two <table>s instead — a header-
only table in a wrapper with no overflow-x-auto ancestor (so
`sticky top-16` correctly sticks to the real page), and a body-only
table that owns the one real horizontal scrollbar, with a scroll
listener mirroring its scrollLeft onto the header. table-layout: fixed
with an identical <colgroup> in both keeps every column pixel-aligned
between them. Role-column headers now wrap (2-3 lines) instead of
truncating, since the whole point is staying able to read which
column is which while scrolled down; Name and Primary Role truncate
with a title tooltip instead, matching this app's existing convention
for per-row text that can't wrap sensibly.

build in a headless-browser repro: the header and the frozen Name

and the two guards racing each other in an unpredictable order could
navigate away before the child ever got to render — landing back on

Fix current-rate resolution picking a stale duplicate salary entry

Same root cause as the earlier salary.ts fix, but duplicated inline in
two more places that don't go through entryEffectiveOn at all:
AccountingDashboard.tsx's Payroll table (latestCompMap) and
ReportAccounting.tsx's current-period/department-breakdown calcs
(latestRateMap, x2). All three took "first row per profile after
ORDER BY effective_date DESC" as the current rate — with no secondary
sort and no tie-break, a same-day duplicate (re-editing a day's rate
inserts a new row rather than replacing one) could win arbitrarily
over a newer correction.

Both queries now also select created_at and sort by it as a tiebreaker,
and the map-building logic explicitly prefers the most recently created
entry on a tie. ReportAccounting.tsx's two copies of the same buggy loop
are consolidated into one buildLatestRateMap() helper.

Fix salary rate edits silently not taking effect on a repeatedly-edited day

Editing a day's rate always INSERTS a new salary_entries row rather than
updating one in place, so re-editing the same day more than once leaves
several rows tied on the same effective_date. entryEffectiveOn()'s
tie-break (entry.effectiveDate > best.effectiveDate) never fires for a
tie, so it kept whichever duplicate row it happened to hit first in an
arbitrarily-ordered query result — a fresh edit could insert correctly
but still lose to a stale duplicate on redisplay, making the edit look
like it silently didn't save.

Now breaks ties by createdAt (the most recently entered correction for
a given day wins), and getSalaryHistory/getCompanySalaryEntries add
created_at as an explicit secondary sort so the fetch order itself is
deterministic too, not just the JS-side resolution.

fix: mobile route map's zoom control and expand/close button hidden behind header

Both bugs had the same root cause: the fixed app header (z-index: 40)
sits at the true top of the screen, and when the map is expanded it also
goes position:fixed/inset:0 to the true top - so the header visually
covers whatever the map places in that first ~52px band.

- Leaflet's top-left zoom control (the "+" button specifically, being
  above "-" in the stack) was rendering right where the header sits.
  Pushed it below the header height + safe-area-inset when expanded.
- The Expand/Close pill had the same problem in expanded mode, but for a
  different reason: it used env(safe-area-inset-top, 0.55rem) as its
  position, assuming the 0.55rem fallback would apply on ordinary
  (non-notched) devices. It doesn't - env()'s fallback only kicks in
  when the browser doesn't support the variable at all, and virtually
  every non-notched device (including desktop Chrome/DevTools) defines
  it as a real 0px. So the fallback never actually applied and the
  button sat flush at the true top edge, fully behind the header.
  Fixed by adding the header height explicitly instead of relying on
  env()'s fallback to provide it.
- Also made the pill itself bigger and higher-contrast (larger padding/
  font, more opaque background, higher z-index) so it's unmistakable
  regardless of screen size or zoom.

Verified in a real headless-Chromium repro built from the actual
production markup/CSS/Leaflet, in both normal and expanded states.

fix: admins created via SuperAdmin now get a working Supabase profile

Two compounding bugs, found while investigating why a brand-new
company's Manager dropdown had nothing to select even though it had
an Admin:

1. createUserAccount() (SuperAdmin's Add Admin flow) created the new
   admin's Firebase Auth credential on the PRIMARY auth instance.
   createUserWithEmailAndPassword always switches that instance's
   current user to the newly created one - so creating a new admin
   was silently signing the calling SuperAdmin out of their own
   session and signing them in as the admin they just created. Fixed
   by moving it onto a secondary Firebase app, the same pattern
   already established in supabase/users.ts's createCompanyUser().

2. createUserAccount() only ever wrote to Firestore - the new admin
   never got a Supabase profile. Since every RLS policy resolves the
   caller's company through profiles (auth_company_id()), an admin
   with no profile can log in but sees no tickets/users/anything
   Supabase-backed - including not showing up as an eligible manager
   candidate for their own company's "add user" form.

- New createSupabaseAdminProfile() in supabase/users.ts, called right
  after createUserAccount() succeeds. Unlike createCompanyUser() (which
  auto-stamps the CALLER's own company), this explicitly targets
  whatever company SuperAdmin picked - verified via a real minted
  SuperAdmin JWT that profiles_insert's RLS (company_id = auth_company_id()
  OR is_superadmin()) allows this cross-company insert.
- Backfilled Supabase profiles for the 3 admins already created this
  way with none (UIC's two attempts, COMP1781626280949's one) -
  confirmed they now appear correctly scoped to their real company.

fix: admin users created via SuperAdmin could vanish from the list

Root cause of "the admin I created for UIC isn't showing but it can
log in": createUserAccount() writes the role-grouped users/{role}/
{status}/{name} record (plus its users_index/{uid} mirror) with fields
named documentId and name - but the UserAccount type (and every read
site: getUserAccount, getUserByUsername, getCompanyUsers, getAllUsers,
getUsersByRole) expects uid and displayName, matching only the OLDER
legacy flat users/{uid} shape. Casting raw Firestore data straight to
UserAccount doesn't rename fields, so every user created via the
newer path came back with uid === undefined.

superadmin.tsx renders the User Accounts table with `key={admin.uid}`.
Two users with the same undefined key collide - React silently drops
one of them instead of erroring. That's exactly what happened: UIC
has two admin records (both from testing321@gmail.com and
testing4321@gmail.com signup attempts), so only one ever rendered.

Login still worked despite this, because auth.tsx's Firestore-fallback
path never reads .uid or .displayName off the profile - it already has
the Firebase uid from the auth listener itself, and only reads role/
companyId/isActive/email, all of which were never mismatched.

fix: NSA credentials never actually reached the deployed Worker

The just-deployed /api/nsa route fix surfaced a second, deeper bug: the
live endpoint returned "NSA credentials not configured" even though
NSA_API_KEY/NSA_SECRET are correctly baked in via vite.config.ts's
SERVER_DEFINE at build time — the same mechanism Supabase/ServicePower/
Marcone credentials already use successfully in production.

Root cause: nsaBridge.ts read credentials through a local alias —
`const g = globalThis as any; ... g.__NSA_API_KEY__` — but vite's define
(esbuild define under the hood) only does an exact textual match on the
literal `globalThis.__NSA_API_KEY__` expression. Through the `g` alias
it never matches, so the substitution silently never happens; the code
falls through to evaluating the real `globalThis.__NSA_API_KEY__` at
runtime, which nothing ever sets (that's the entire point of using
define — there's no other mechanism to set it), so it's always
undefined. Confirmed directly in the built output before this fix:
`g.__NSA_API_KEY__` was still present as literal, unsubstituted source
in the deployed bundle.

NSA has no working fallback for this (unlike the working bridges,
NSA_API_KEY/NSA_SECRET have never been set as real Cloudflare secrets —
confirmed earlier this session via `wrangler secret list`), so this
bug was fully exposed rather than masked.

jotformBridge.ts has the exact same `const g = globalThis as any`
aliasing pattern for 8 of its own secrets — fixed it too, even though
it "works" today, since that's only because its specific secrets (SA
private key, Supabase service key, Jotform API key) DO have real
Cloudflare secrets configured as a working fallback. That's a
coincidence of which secrets happen to be double-configured, not
something the code should depend on — same latent bug, just not yet
exposed.

Verified against the actual built bundle, not just tsc: before the fix,
`__NSA_API_KEY__`/`__FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID__`/`__JOTFORM_API_KEY__` were
all still present as literal unreplaced text in dist/server's vendor
chunk; after, none are. Booted the fixed build via wrangler dev and
confirmed a live getDispatch call for AAN20260736483522 now succeeds
end-to-end instead of returning the credentials error.

fix: make the dist/ pre-build cleanup self-heal on Windows EBUSY

The EBUSY fix from earlier (clean dist/ ourselves at config-load time,
disable emptyOutDir) assumed nothing else was holding a lock on the
directory at that exact moment — but a leftover workerd process from an
earlier build or test run can still be alive right then, and the plain
rmSync call itself hit the same EBUSY error, just relocated to a
different point (config load instead of Vite's internal build step).

mechanism for exactly this class of transient Windows lock, instead of
failing on the first hit. Stress-tested with 3 full builds run back to
back with zero manual process cleanup in between (previously guaranteed
to fail); all 3 succeeded.

fix: branch resolution matching city names across state lines

Found via HAP20260736477959: a customer in Villa Ridge, MO (zip 63089,
a St. Louis suburb) got assigned to the Cape Girardeau branch instead —
136.9mi away instead of the real ~36mi. Root cause was two-fold:

1. Zip 63089 was simply missing from the static ZIP_COVERAGE table,
   despite both its immediate neighbors (63088 Valley Park, 63099
   Fenton) being mapped to St. Louis. Added the missing entry.
2. resolveBranchFromCustomer()'s loose city-name fallback (used when a
   zip has no exact match) compared city names only, with no state
   check. It matched "Villa Ridge" against a completely unrelated real
   town of the same name in the table — Villa Ridge, IL (zip 62996,
   ~250mi from Villa Ridge, MO) — and confidently returned the wrong
   branch. This isn't specific to NSA; it's the shared fallback used by
   both the NSA and ServicePower sync paths, so any customer whose city
   name happens to collide with a different-state city already in the
   table was at risk of the same silent misassignment.

Added a standard USPS zip3-prefix-to-state table (stateFromZip5) and
gated the loose match on it: an entry is only accepted if its own zip
resolves to the same state as the customer's. Falls back to the old
unguarded city-only match when the customer's state can't be determined
at all, rather than returning nothing. Exported normalizeStateCode
(already existed, wasn't exported) to normalize the customer's state
for this comparison.

Verified live: Villa Ridge, MO -> St. Louis (was Cape Girardeau);
Villa Ridge, IL still correctly -> Cape Girardeau, confirming the guard
doesn't just reject the city outright. Mileage isn't stored — it's
computed live from ticket.location, so patching HAP20260736477959's
location to St. Louis in Supabase self-corrects the mileage display.

fix: same date-only UTC parsing bug in Certificate of Employment generator

Same root cause as New Ticket's schedule date bug: employeeStartDate and
the certificate's own date field came from <input type="date"> values,
reformatted via new Date(str).toLocaleDateString() — which parses a
date-only ISO string as UTC midnight, then rolls it back a day when
rendered in any US timezone. Would have silently printed the wrong date
on a real HR document. Replaced with plain string slicing.

feat: dedicated Case Number column, persist NSA fields, cancellation-reason dropdown

Case Number gets its own tickets.case_number column (migration 0056),
separate from original_ticket_no ("Redo Ticket #"). The two used to

field), which meant a ticket could never have both, and the ticket
