the redo flag. Existing rows are backfilled: any ticket with a value in
original_ticket_no but redo = false gets it moved to case_number. New
Ticket gets a "Case Number (Optional)" field next to Source/Name,
wired to the new column.

Along the way, found that NSA dispatch sync was silently dropping the
case number and a dozen other NSA-specific fields (status, route,
group, deductible, schedule ack, special instructions, coverage,
pre-auth, master code) — nsaSync.ts computed them from the dispatch
response, but upsertTicketFromServicePowerImpl() had no handling for
any of it, so they never reached Supabase. The ticket detail page only
ever showed them correctly via a separate live re-fetch straight from
the NSA API on every page view — invisible everywhere else (Work Map,
Ticket List, reports). Migration 0055 adds the columns; tickets.ts now
actually reads/writes them.

Also wires up the cancellation-reason dropdown on the ticket detail
page's visit log: selecting "CL-Need Cancel" now requires a reason
(from operationsBranchMetrics.ts's CANCEL_REASONS), which gets appended
to the ticket's Internal Note.

Fixes a date-only-string parsing bug in New Ticket along the way: New
Ticket's <input type="date"> value was being reformatted via
`new Date(str).toLocaleDateString()`, which parses a date-only ISO
string as UTC midnight — rendering it back out in any US timezone
(behind UTC) rolls the date back a day, so a Cx Preferred Date of July
7 was silently saved as July 6. Replaced with plain string slicing that
never touches a Date object.

fix: Leaflet SSR crash, circular chunk crash, and geocode cache bugs

- Lazy-load Leaflet (JS + CSS) behind a dynamic import instead of a
  static one — Leaflet touches `window` at module load time, which was
  crashing the Cloudflare Workers SSR build (no `window` there) since
  every map-bearing page is server-rendered.
- Give Leaflet its own Rollup chunk and disable hoistTransitiveImports
  quirks that were still pulling it into the eagerly-evaluated bundle
  despite the dynamic import.
- Merge the "app-lib" chunk into "vendor" to eliminate a genuine
  circular chunk dependency (introduced by the angelo merge, not this
  work) that was causing `Cannot access 'X' before initialization`
  crashes in production.
- Fix geocode_cache writes: the upsert's onConflict target didn't match
  the table's actual unique constraint, and the payload never set
  company_id — every fresh geocode was silently failing to cache and
  re-hitting Geoapify/Google on every lookup. Migration backfills the
  default so existing callers don't need to change their payload.
- Cache the company map provider setting and the geocoder's in-memory
  cache at module scope instead of re-fetching/re-creating them on
  every page mount — real, measurable chunk of the "map feels slow"
  delay.

Load module access gates before first render so tiles respect role restrictions

Role-gate overrides were hydrated fire-and-forget after login, so on a

Fix role-preview tile flash: read extraRoles from useAuth, not a real-account DB fetch

m.$module.tsx (the mobile module tile grid) fetched extraRoles via a
separate getMyRoles(uid) call starting from [], which always resolved to the
REAL signed-in account's own secondary roles - ignoring an active "View as"
role preview entirely. The grid rendered correctly filtered for the
previewed role on first paint (using the initial []), then a moment later
the fetch landed with the real account's broader secondary roles and
re-filtered against those, "populating" in tiles the previewed role should
never see.

synchronously alongside role, and correctly forced to [] during a preview),
matching the pattern m.$module.$submodule.tsx already used. Applied the same
fix to ItTicketsPage.tsx, LiveChatSupportPage.tsx, and
useMergedNotifications.ts, which had the identical getMyRoles(uid) race.

Fix payroll numbers changing on reopen and require re-toggling to sync

Roughly a dozen period-scoped bulk loads in AccountingDashboard.tsx (attendance,
tech repair/assigned counts, mileage, custom pay items, category overrides,
holidays, hourly/OT overrides) each fired their own request independently with
no coordination, so opening a technician's payroll detail mid-cascade computed
off whatever partial combination of data happened to be loaded at that instant
— a different "snapshot" each time depending on network timing, not a real
change in the underlying numbers. Added a periodDataLoading counter that all of
these (plus the three ad-hoc refreshes triggered by editing a custom line,
training value, or category count from inside the Tech Activity Report modal)
now increment/decrement, and gate the technician name link so it can't be
opened until every one of them has actually settled.

Also fixes payroll_hourly_ot_overrides storing a frozen dollar amount instead
of a live mode: once Finance selected "State" pay mode, the saved figure never
updated again even after later edits changed the true state-matched total,
requiring a manual re-toggle to force a fresh save. TechActivityReportModal now
auto-resaves the override whenever the live State total and the saved amount
have actually drifted apart — gated on periodDataSettling so it never fires off
a transitional, mid-refetch value.

Also compresses the Tech Activity Report's Hourly Pay row to 3 decimal places,
matching the Payroll Detail modal's existing precision.

(cherry picked from commit 779019df6ffa6f4728246d8b29736ccdf6269f0a)

Show LDT as its own row and include it in Total Payment

LDT (ldtCount/ldtPay, tech_manual_pay_items) already correctly factored

Fix guaranteed-minimum-salary match double-counting the state floor match

techGuaranteedSalaryMatch was checked against techHourlyPayCompanyOnly
(the un-overridden flat calc) even when a State-mode override was active,
on the theory that the state-floor match is separate money the guarantee
shouldn't get to absorb. That reasoning doesn't hold: when techHourlyPay
is the State-mode figure, it already has the state match folded in, so
adding a guarantee sized against the smaller Company-only baseline paid
that same state match twice (see Matthew Nichols: a $60k salary floor
plus a real state-floor shortfall together overstated Total Payment on
the Office Employee Payroll list by exactly his $199.88 state match,
$2,761.28 shown vs the correct $2,561.39 the Tech Activity Report and
reference payroll workbook both already agreed on).

Now keyed off techHourlyPay (whichever mode is actually applied) instead.
If State-mode earnings already clear the salary target, the match is
correctly $0 and the technician keeps the full higher state-matched
amount; if they still fall short, the guarantee tops up only the
remaining gap instead of re-adding money already earned.
(cherry picked from commit 9877298ee157c0139ea397aacf233719d37bf588)

Fix race condition saving the Company/State Hourly+OT override too early

The Company/State toggle buttons on the Tech Activity Report were only
disabled while the save itself (hourlyOtModeBusy) was in flight -- not
while loadingStateComparison (the per-day attendance/state fetch that
computes stateMinFloor, matchMin, and stateHourlyOtTotal) was still
running. Clicking State before that fetch settled saved whatever
stateHourlyOtTotal happened to be at that exact moment, sometimes
computed from incomplete data, permanently baking a wrong number into
payroll_hourly_ot_overrides (see Bradley Hollowell conversation, where
this produced three different wrong totals across repeated clicks).

Now both buttons are also disabled while loadingStateComparison is true,
so a click can only ever capture the fully-settled, correct total.
(cherry picked from commit a819c1ee700d279e27c49e16d9af9c9e5da9f351)

Stop the per-day state edit from wiping the whole dashboard

The debounce added earlier only delayed the full-page reload, it never
addressed the cause: fetchData() sets loading=true, and
"if (loading) return <BrandedLoader/>" unmounts the entire dashboard --
including the modal being edited -- behind a blocking spinner. Clicking
through several "State Not Assigned" days in a row could even stagger
multiple wipes if each edit's own network round-trip ate into the 800ms
debounce window, which is why it looked worse, not better.

Give fetchData a silent option that skips the loading flag, matching the
"targeted refresh, not fetchData()" pattern already established here for
refreshTechRepairRates. onRateChanged now calls fetchData({ silent: true }),
so a state edit refreshes company-wide totals in the background without
closing the modal or blanking the screen.
(cherry picked from commit bc15e6437d038177c0296cc0dd25919476f53623)

Debounce the dashboard refresh triggered by per-day state edits

onRateChanged triggers a full company-wide reload (all profiles, salary
entries, payroll line items, audit log, PTO, mileage, etc.), so firing it
immediately on every single state-dropdown selection reloaded the whole
accounting dashboard once per click -- painful when clearing several
"State Not Assigned" days in a row. Coalesce rapid edits into one refresh
800ms after the last change, and flush any pending refresh on unmount so
closing the modal right after an edit doesn't leave stale totals behind.
(cherry picked from commit 5f9d96c5809084c1fdfffed328719fc11514d5fe)

  location…" spinner cycling forever once GPS has given up.

Timecard reset:
- saveEntry re-writes all five punch columns from the client's in-memory
  copy every save. A transient read failure in the field left the clock
  card blank; the tech re-tapped Time In and the save upserted NULL over
  the real check-in. New savePunch() does a single-column upsert so a
  stale local view can't erase sibling punches; the mobile Home and
  Timecard clock surfaces both use it.
- A failed timecard load now shows "couldn't load — retry" with the
  buttons disabled, instead of a blank card that looks like a fresh day
  (which also produced the misleading "please re-login" alert).
- getMonthEntries / getEntryForDate / the getMyProfileSchedule profile
  lookup now retry genuine network blips, like saveEntry already did.

Fix on-site check-in GPS deadlock; harden timecard against stray taps; add server-synced header clock

- HomeOnSiteCard: precise-GPS refinement was scoped to focusTickets, which
  stays pinned to a single in-progress ticket once Work Start is tapped —
  starving GPS refinement for the next job and leaving distance checks
  against a stale/coarse fix. Reported by a tech who could never check in
  to a second ticket after finishing the first. Now scans all pending
  tickets so refinement never stalls.
- MobileTimecardView: Time In/Out and Meal In/Out now arm on first tap and
  require a confirming second tap, matching the Home card's pattern — a
  stray tap could previously end a shift instantly with no way back.
- MobileHomeView: Time/Meal punches now stamp with the server-verified
  clock (getServerNow) instead of the device clock, closing the same gap
  already closed on the Timecard tab.
- New header clock (server-synced, shown in the technician's own
  schedule_timezone) so the app always shows a trustworthy reference time.

Geocoding fallback chain for addresses the geocoders can't place

Rural addresses (e.g. 109 BRONCO RDG PLEASANTON TX, 80 S Nixon Ave Nixon
TX) wouldn't geocode at all — abbreviated street types the geocoders
don't expand, plus sparse small-town street data — so the tech had no
map point and couldn't check in.

makeGeocoder now runs a fallback chain instead of giving up on the first
null:
- expand the uncommon USPS abbreviations that actually trip geocoders
  (RDG->RIDGE, HWY->HIGHWAY, XING, HOLW, CO RD->COUNTY ROAD, CR <n>, a
  leading directional after the house number…) — NOT the everyday
  RD/ST/AVE/DR ones, since expanding "ST" would break "ST CHARLES";
- retry on the other provider (Google mode -> Geoapify when keyed;
  Leaflet mode stays Google-free by design);
- coarsen: full address -> street centroid -> city -> ZIP centroid
  (zippopotam), each flagged `approximate`;
- fold in the provider's own fuzzy signal (Google partial_match /
  APPROXIMATE, Geoapify street/postcode/city result_type or low
  confidence).

Only address-precise hits are written to the shared geocode_cache — a ZIP
centroid must not become "the address" for every caller.

New `geocodeAddress()` returns the precision flag; `makeGeocoder()` stays
a `LatLng | null` wrapper so every existing map/route caller transparently
gains the fallbacks. The On-Site Check-In card uses `geocodeAddress`: an
approximate anchor never hard-passes the geofence and never triggers GPS
refinement — it routes straight to the manual "I'm here anyway" override,
whose logged comment now notes "(address only approximately mapped)".

On-Site Check-In: multi-ticket picker + manual "I'm here anyway" override

Two follow-ups to the GPS-accuracy fix.

Picker: the card no longer snaps to a single nearest ticket. It now lists
every ticket the tech can act on — the ones already checked in (not yet
done) plus every not-yet-started ticket inside the geofence — sorted
nearest-first, capped at 5 rows. With the 400 m radius, two customers
within ~800 m produce overlapping zones, and several appliances routinely
share one address; auto-snapping to whichever centroid read nearest could
check the tech into the wrong customer's ticket. Now they pick.

Manual override: when the automatic check rejects a ticket the tech is
genuinely at — address interpolated to the wrong point on a rural road,
GPS that never sharpened, or an address that wouldn't geocode at all — an
"I'm here anyway" button appears, but only within
ON_SITE_CHECKIN_MANUAL_OVERRIDE_MAX_MILES (3 mi) or when there's no
geocode to measure against, so it can't double as "check in from home".
It confirms, then writes the same onsite_arrived_at plus a ticket comment
recording what the check *did* measure ("manual override — GPS placed me
about 1.4 mi from the address"), so dispatch can see and sanity-check it.

Fix On-Site Check-In gate: use real GPS, not the coarse shared fix

Technicians standing at the customer's door couldn't tap Work Start —
the card showed them "1.2 mi away". The geofence test used the position
from TechnicianLocationTracker's shared watcher, which runs at
enableHighAccuracy:false (cell-tower / Wi-Fi, routinely 1 km+ off) — fine
for the dispatch breadcrumb, useless for a "you must be here" check
against a 200 m circle.

- The On-Site Check-In card now takes its own one-shot high-accuracy
  getCurrentPosition on a 12s interval while there's an un-checked-in
  focus ticket, and uses that (when fresh, <45s) for the distance test.
  One-shot, so no second always-on watchPosition; stops the moment Work
  Start is tapped or the ticket is done; only for a clocked-in tech who's
  confirmed location sharing.
- The geofence now adds the fix's own reported accuracy as slack, capped
  at 250 m so a coarse "±3 km" fix can't widen it to nothing. accuracy is
  now carried on liveLocationContext.
- Base radius 200 m -> 400 m: address geocoding interpolates the street
  number along a road segment and on rural/highway addresses lands the
  pin hundreds of metres (sometimes >1 mi) off the building.
- Card shows "Getting precise location…" while a fix is in flight instead
  of a misleading coarse "1.2 mi away", and the button reads "Locating…".

Let HR reset a locked-out user's password to the default

The "Default" button on User Management already showed for HR (HR is in
USER_MANAGEMENT_ROLES), but /api/admin-reset-password only allowed
ADMIN/SUPERADMIN and only checked the caller's primary role, so HR got a
403. Add HR to the allowed set and match it against the primary role OR
any extra_roles entry, so a held secondary HR role qualifies too.
Company scoping and the single-target / known-default constraints are
unchanged.

Speed up Ticket List load: concurrent paging, page-scoped column enrichment

The Ticket List took ~1 min to open once the company's ticket table grew
past a few thousand rows. Three things caused it:

- getCompanyTickets() paged the whole table 1000 rows at a time but
  serially (await per page).
- TicketList then ran two more whole-table passes to derive the Part
  Order and Triage Notes columns, each sending a ~3.4k-element .in(...)
  filter — which PostgREST silently caps at 1000 rows, so both columns
  were also wrong for most tickets once visits/parts passed 1000.
- syncApprovedPortalRequests() was awaited before the first ticket fetch
  on every page open.

Changes:
- getCompanyTickets(): first page + exact count in one request, remaining
  pages fetched concurrently. Deterministic order via an id tiebreaker
  (created_at is not unique after a bulk import, so range() paging could
  drop/duplicate rows across page boundaries).
- TicketList: derive Part Order + Triage Notes for the visible page only
  (~25 ids), cached per id, batched with a concurrency cap for "Show:
  All". Fixes the slowdown and the 1000-row truncation bug.
- TicketList: run the portal-request sync in the background; only reload
  the list if it actually pulled something.
- New index idx_tickets_company_created (company_id, created_at desc,
  id desc) matching the list's sort/paging path.

Fix RLS: company-scoped Super Admin couldn't see live technician GPS pings

is_admin() or is_superadmin() meant 'Admin or company Super Admin' before
0099_role_hierarchy_split.sql split SUPERADMIN into platform-level
SUPERSUPERADMIN and company-scoped SUPERADMIN. After that split
is_superadmin() only matches the platform role, so a company Super Admin
silently got zero rows back on technician_location_pings (RLS-empty, not
an error) while Admin worked fine. Swaps in is_company_superadmin() on
both the SELECT and DELETE policies.
Accept .jfif photo uploads (same decode path as .jpg, no HEIC-style conversion needed)

originally reported and audited every caller of getCompanyUsers() (51

Notification-routing bugs (not a visible list, but the same root cause —

Fix Admin-module tile grid ignoring secondary roles; server-verify manager proxy clock-ins; fix stale-token uploads on every signable HR form

m.$module.tsx's own extraRoles fetch only ran for the Dashboard module, so
every other module's tile grid (including Admin) always filtered against
an empty extra_roles array. This was invisible before canAccessSubmodule
started properly gating the Admin module here too, at which point anyone
whose Admin access came only from a secondary role lost every Admin tile
except the ones with their own primary-role carve-out (e.g. IT Tickets).
Fetch extraRoles for every module now; also fixes an isAdmin check
elsewhere in the same file with the identical gap.

Manager proxy clock-in (AttendanceMonitoringPage.tsx's desktop button and
MobileTechApp.tsx's "Clock In Team" view) still used the browser/phone's
own clock — same class of issue as the self-punch fix already shipped.
nowInTimezone() now optionally takes a server-verified instant; both
proxy flows pass one in. Also found and fixed the technician's own
Time In/Out in MobileTechApp.tsx itself, which had the original
client-clock bug and was missed in the first pass.

Separately: a multi-upload HR form (Employee Data: SSN card, driver's
license front+back, signature, then the final PDF) failed with
"storage/unauthorized" on the last upload — a slow connection let the
Firebase ID token backing the Storage SDK go stale partway through the
sequence, even though the user was still genuinely signed in. Added
refreshStorageAuthToken() (forces a fresh token before a form's upload
sequence) and applied it everywhere the same multi-upload pattern exists:
every Fill*Page.tsx signable form, the shared Sign*Page.tsx components,
and HR's own 7 co-signature dialogs in ReportHRDaily.tsx.

Lock time-clock punches to a server-verified clock; hide restricted modules from listing surfaces

Time In/Out and Meal In/Out (both the header quick-punch buttons and My
Timecard's day modal) previously stamped with the browser's own Date(),
so an employee could set their computer's clock back or forward to fake a
punch time. Added a real /api/server-time endpoint (Cloudflare's own
system clock, wired into both prod and local dev) and a client helper
that converts that server instant into the employee's own scheduled
timezone (profiles.schedule_timezone, the same field the header clock and
Master List's Hours of Work dropdown already use) before stamping a
punch. Also moved My Timecard's "only today" edit gate onto the same
server-verified date, closing a similar clock-manipulation path there.

Separately: three listing surfaces (the Welcome-back module cards, the
header's quick-switch dropdown, and a module's own tile grid) were only
checking the CSR department allow-list, missing the admin-module/user-
management/activity-log/company-settings gates the actual submodule
route enforces — so a restricted item could show up in these lists and
then hit "Access restricted" once opened. Extracted the route's full gate
logic into a shared canAccessSubmodule() (submoduleAccess.ts) and wired
all three surfaces to it; the route's own enforcement is untouched, only
its role-list constants moved to the shared file so the two can't drift.

Fix Employee Confidentiality submitted PDF: wrong drawRectangle keys were blanking out most of the form

BRANCH_PLACEHOLDER_COVER used {w, h} but pdf-lib's drawRectangle() only
recognizes {width, height} — the mismatch silently fell back to pdf-lib's
own default (150x100) instead of the intended small 256x24 cover box. That
oversized rectangle, anchored at the Branch line, painted over Zip/State/
City, Address, and part of Full Name too, erasing real submitted values.
Verified by generating and rendering test PDFs through the actual code
path until the exact cause was isolated. Also re-measured all field
coordinates against the real PDF text positions (same measurement used to
fix the live-fill overlay's coordinates).

Fix build errors after adopting rulonajhon/darkglass-hub-suite baseline; fix Employee Confidentiality form overlay

Zero out the 106 tsc errors inherited from the adopted codebase: wire up

Primary role is display/title/hierarchy only — it must never be the sole

Fixes the same missing-extra_roles gap across 14 files: manager-assignment
dropdown, CV-forward and COE-signer recipient lists, Claims/Parts staff
rosters, #announcements posting, stage-1 conduct-note review, login-email
edit permission, bulk schedule eligibility, mobile self-view routing,

admin roster/count (verified live: was missing real admins holding ADMIN
only as a secondary role).

Overhaul Triage Daily Report: TR- stage/aging, staff table, Activity & Attendance
